name: 1.5 Data Collection Experiment - Lab
_note: Built 2026-08-26. All sixteen authored fresh (lab kind, second lab manifest in the -SH book): systematic-sampling-positions, why-twelve-distinct-marks, systematic-versus-srs, ungrouped-table-blanks, cumulative-relative-frequency-named-row, grouped-table-blanks, at-most-two/more-than-two (ungrouped-only cuts), at-most-three/more-than-three (boundary cuts, either table), grouping-hides-the-question, bottom-row-cumulative-check, camila-vs-rosa-settlement, why-switch-tables, grouping-the-data-differently, pre-frq-grade-a-table-comparison. Points 15x6 + 10 = 100. BookSHelf 1.5 is the Data Collection Experiment lab: systematic sample of 12 classmates, 60 movie counts, both frequency tables, four at-most/more-than questions, Camila-vs-Rosa, three discussion questions. The MOM assignment mirrors the whole lab with per-student randomized 60-count datasets (frequencies are multiples of 3, so every relative frequency is exact and the bottom cumulative is exactly 1) and auto-grades every part; the four 'which table and why' questions are structurally identical across datasets (cut at 2 = ungrouped only, cut at 3 = either). Lab settings per reference/intro-stats-assessment-settings.md: 3 attempts x 20 versions, no penalty, no early-finish bonus, GROUP gradebook category, 2 late passes, no time limit. Pre-FRQ is authored-first (no lab FRQ to mirror): categories Defensible Position (3) / Evidence from Your Own Tables (4) / Addresses Grouping Tradeoffs (3), dropped category ADDRESSES GROUPING TRADEOFFS.

questions.title: Systematic Sampling Positions - mark the 12 positions on a numbered list by stepping by 4 from a random start, wrapping back to the top at the bottom
Why Twelve Distinct Marks - a 24-name list and a step of 4 visit only 6 names before the pattern repeats
Systematic Versus Simple Random - exactly one random decision in the whole procedure, and why that makes it systematic
Ungrouped Frequency Table Blanks - back-solve a blanked frequency from the total 60 and read two relative frequencies off the completed class table
Cumulative Relative Frequency at a Named Row - read one cumulative cell off the completed ungrouped table instead of adding the column by hand
Grouped Frequency Table Blanks - back-solve a blanked group frequency and two group relative frequencies from the same 60 movie counts
At Most Two Which Table - the proportion at most 2, then which table shows it and why
At Most Three Which Table - the proportion at most 3, then which table shows it and why
More Than Two Which Table - the share above 2 by complement, then which table shows it and why
More Than Three Which Table - the share above 3 by complement, then which table shows it and why
Grouping Hides the Question - why a grouped table cannot answer more than two, and what the answer actually needs
Bottom-Row Cumulative Check - a miscounted table whose bottom cumulative is not 1; find the drop, name the row, fix the bottom
Camila vs Rosa Settlement - more than three from both tables gives the same share, and the boundary explains why
Why Switch Tables - which of the four questions forces a switch to the ungrouped table, and when staying is fine
Grouping the Data Differently - a legal regrouping of the same 60 counts and what a different grouping can and cannot change
Pre-FRQ Grade a Table Comparison - The scenario and grading checklist of the table-comparison FRQ, but the student grades four sample responses against the rubric instead of writing one
